title: The Groovy Seventies
tagline: Jumbo jets, the first Earth Day and colour TV in the living room.

locale.persona: a young family in a California suburb

morningRoutine.detail: Colour sets were spreading fast; 1972 was the first year more than half of TV households had one.

source.label: Wikipedia: Color television

morningRoutine.activity: Drive to work on the freeway
morningRoutine.detail: Big sedans and station wagons on the freeway, with gasoline at about 36 cents a gallon.

source.label: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Annual Energy Review, Table 5.24: Retail Motor Gasoline and On-Highway Diesel Fuel Prices, 1949–2011

morningRoutine.detail: Suburban children rode buses to large consolidated schools; fewer than 2,000 one-teacher schools were left in the country.

source.label: NCES, 120 Years of American Education: A Statistical Portrait (1993), Table 20

places.description: Jumbo jets, a near-disaster in space, and an estimated 20 million Americans turning out for the first Earth Day.

technology.name: Boeing 747
technology.description: The first wide-body "jumbo jet" entered service on January 22, 1970, on Pan Am's New York–London route.

source.label: Wikipedia: Boeing 747

technology.name: Colour television
technology.description: Colour set sales overtook black-and-white in 1972; in 1970 colour was becoming the norm.

source.label: Wikipedia: Color television

technology.name: Countertop microwave oven
technology.description: Introduced as a countertop appliance in 1967, the microwave oven was starting its move into home kitchens.

source.label: Wikipedia: Microwave oven

technology.name: Push-button telephone
technology.description: Touch-tone push-button phones, introduced in 1963, offered a faster alternative to the rotary dial.

source.label: Wikipedia: DTMF signaling (Touch-Tone)

futureVisions.prediction: Societies will suffer "future shock": too much change in too short a period of time, with information overload.
futureVisions.whoSaidIt: Alvin Toffler (with Adelaide Farrell), Future Shock (1970)

source.label: Wikipedia: Future Shock

futureVisions.prediction: People will change professions and workplaces often, having many careers in a lifetime.
futureVisions.note: Americans born in 1957–64 held an average of 12.9 jobs between ages 18 and 58, though many stayed in one line of work.

source.label: Wikipedia: Future Shock
